title: Canonical files stored with a .canon suffix to dodge tool auto-discovery
rationale: Biome auto-discovers ANY file named biome.json as a nested root config regardless of files.includes or experimentalScannerIgnores, which fails 'bun run lint' with a nested-root-config error. Storing bytes under a non-discoverable filename is the only clean fix that keeps canonical content pristine — adding root:false would pollute the canonical config that target repos adopt and break json-subset matching. A uniform suffix (vs special-casing biome.json) is future-proof against other auto-discovered names (package.json, tsconfig.json).

title: Drift engine: matcher-driven states with extra=compliant-superset and template at ## granularity
rationale: trellis-ffdd's drift.ts resolves per-file state via DRIFT_STATES match|allowed-delta|drift|missing|extra. Non-obvious calls baked in: (1) 'extra' = a clean SUPERSET — target satisfies every canonical requirement AND adds keys/sections (DivergenceKind 'added'); it is NON-failing alongside match/allowed-delta, while only drift+missing fail (FAILING_DRIFT_STATES, drives future --fail-on drift). (2) json/yaml-subset applies subset semantics to OBJECT KEYS ONLY — arrays and primitives must deep-equal, so extending an array is drift, not extra; widen via an allowedDelta. (3) template matcher (AGENTS.md) compares at top-level ## granularity only — deeper ###+ subsections are finer structure repos reorganize freely; <<TOKEN>> headings act as regex wildcards; a TEMPLATE_SCAFFOLD denylist (/^replaceable tokens$/) drops consumer-removed instructional sections. AllowedDelta whitelists whole-file (paths absent) or structural-path-prefix; only required (non-added) divergences are allow-checked. driftRepo is pure/sync (no wall-clock), folds into report.drift only when AuditOptions.canonical is set so the §6.3 golden shape is unperturbed. Renderers live in drift-report.ts to keep drift.ts under the 400-line ratchet.
